attempts.summary: Configured keepalived (VRRP) on node1 and node2 (OpenWrt 25.12.2, apk-installed) to share virtual IP 10.100.244.50/24 on br-lan, the private network they share with node3 (RHEL 7.9). node1 is MASTER (priority 150), node2 is BACKUP (priority 100), virtual_router_id 51. Demonstrated automatic failover: stopped keepalived on node1, node2 assumed the VIP within ~4s, and a continuous ping from node3 across the transition showed zero packet loss (icmp_seq 1-51 uninterrupted, only a transient ICMP redirect/latency blip, no drops). Restored node1 and the pair returned to its normal MASTER/BACKUP state (node1 preempts back due to higher priority). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node1, then node2, then node3), each verified via a changed OS boot_id and post-restart proof: keepalived auto-started (enabled) and VRRP state/VIP placement recovered correctly on node1/node2, and node3 regained ping connectivity to the VIP after its own restart. Final state: node1 MASTER holding VIP, node2 clean BACKUP, node3 pinging VIP with 0% loss.
